Subaru Tests Longtail WRX at the Nurburgring, but What Could It Be?
20 photos
Photo: Baldauf
The VB-series WRX came out in 2021. A whole bunch of limited editions and performance versions later, the VB could be on its way out. After all, the VA-series WRX came in 2014 and went the way of the dodo in 2021. The big question, however, is whether this black-painted test vehicle is a prototype of yet another VB performance version or a mule of its long-awaited replacement.
Spied testing with minimal camouflage at the world's most grueling racetrack, the mystery WRX appears to don extended rear quarter panels. Those panels extend outward, giving the car a particularly different look from the VB on sale today. A modified rear aerodynamic diffuser can also be seen, and the trunk lid is complemented by a very purposeful spoiler.
Why did Subaru camouflage it so carefully? The only answer to said question is future model development, though what kind of model remains to be seen. If you ask me, I believe that a new generation is on the horizon. The timing is right for such a move, and rather than coming up with a completely new platform, Subaru is much better off updating the current one.
Beyond the four-door sedan, the next generation is understood to be joined by a hatchback variant. The Japanese manufacturer previewed the hatchback at the 2025 Japan Mobility Show in the form of the Performance-B STI concept, a five-door show car loosely inspired by the hatchback-only Impreza.
Also worth noting, Subaru prepares to reveal the 2027 model year WRX for the Japanese domestic market. While not presented as an entirely new generation, the newcomer has been confirmed to feature an evolution of the heavy-duty STI manual transmission instead of the lesser TY75 box.
Photo: Baldauf Instead of cable operation, the TY85 is a rod-linked unit designed to handle more abuse and higher torque loads. A crack team of engineers discovered that a partner factory was still capable of building TY85 componentry, and that's how the manufacturer decided to revive this row-your-own tranny.
Said TY85-equipped WRX is one of three row-your-own models that Subaru will debut through 2027. The other two include a new version of the BRZ and a five-door hatchback. The latter is expected to be the WRX hatchback revival previewed by the 2025 Japan Mobility Show concept, and the hatchback should use the very same platform and oily bits as the TY85-equipped WRX.
Turning our attention back to the Nurburgring test vehicle, the camouflaged section of the diffuser extends farther rearward. The matching lip spoiler follows a completely new outline, reaching farther behind the trunk. Subaru also concealed the flat openings on either side of the rear bumper, making this vehicle all the more perplexing. All told, it looks like a longtail conversion of the VB.
Due to the lack of a ginormous rear wing and serious braking hardware, this definitely isn't an STI. The Japanese automaker confirmed back in March 2022 that the VB won't receive an STI variant, citing stricter regulations and the changing marketplace for its decision. At the time, Subaru further acknowledged that it's exploring opportunities, including electrification, for the next WRX STI.
